factCheck.text: L0101 'Once, a machine learned to see.'
Place stamp 'Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory · Buffalo, New York · c. 1960'
L0102 'four hundred light cells, twenty by twenty' and the on-screen '400 light cells'
L0103 'wires, and racks of dials that motors turned' (the patch board with tangled cables, then the potentiometer racks and a meter panel)
L0104 'the Mark I Perceptron, the project of psychologist Frank Rosenblatt' and the name card 'Frank Rosenblatt, psychologist'
L0105 'Nobody gave it the rule. Show it a shape; it guesses.'
factCheck.verdict: supported; follows the claim's caveat wording ('nobody gave it the rule', not 'nobody told it the answer'). The 'correct answer: horizontal' card shows honestly that training was supervised.

factCheck.text: L0105b 'Each lit cell tugs the needle through the dials it feeds; the total decides' with the 'threshold' mark and the caption 'an illustration, simplified'
factCheck.verdict: supported. The theatre leaves out the random association layer, and the caption discloses that.

factCheck.text: L0106 'motors nudge the dials that had a say, a little, toward the right answer' (only the dials fed by lit cells move, with arrows)
L0107 tries 1-5 ('said vertical · WRONG' x3, 'try 4 · said vertical · RIGHT', 'try 5 · a new horizontal bar · said horizontal · RIGHT')
factCheck.verdict: internally consistent trial-and-error trace; try 5 shows a new bar, so it generalises rather than memorises

factCheck.text: L0108 'It could learn only simple patterns' with 'what it could learn: simple patterns' (vertical and horizontal plates)
factCheck.verdict: supported as plain English for linearly separable

factCheck.text: 'In 1969, Minsky and Papert showed just how simple' with '1969 · Minsky & Papert, Perceptrons' and the 'XOR · one lit, not both … never settles' mini machine
factCheck.verdict: supported; the XOR unit is a two-input single-layer machine, which is exactly the claim's scope
fair, though less hedged than the source ('often thought to have contributed to a decline'). The line does not assert causation; see the fairness notes.

factCheck.text: 'Its descendants, today's neural networks, still learn from mistakes'
factCheck.verdict: supported at the level stated (error-driven weight adjustment). It does not claim that the algorithm is the same.

fairnessNotes: Minsky and Papert are treated fairly. The film credits them with a demonstration ('showed just how simple'), not with an attack, and the limit is shown on a single-layer unit, as the limit-linear caveat requires. Nothing suggests they proved neural networks useless, and the 'descendants' line immediately reopens the lineage.

The causal link between the book and the decline is implied by juxtaposition (semicolon, then the dim), not stated. That is within the source's 'often thought to have contributed' and acceptable for a one-minute film. A longer cut would need the hedge said aloud.

Rosenblatt is depicted with dignity: a planted, attentive figure at the patch board and beside the eye, named once with his correct profession, and with no invented biography, quotes or dialogue. Quotes.json is empty, and the film has no quotes, as the brief requires.
No geopolitics, funding bodies or rival labs are mentioned, so there is no even-handedness exposure. The Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory and Buffalo are named correctly.

The on-screen teaching apparatus discloses that it is an illustration ('an illustration, simplified'), which keeps the vertical/horizontal bars from being taken as the Mark I's historical task (the cited demo was X versus E).
best_moments: 52.1-57.8 s: '1969' appears as it is spoken, then 'Minsky & Papert, Perceptrons' (italic title) beside a legible closed book, while the XOR mini machine's check/cross row 'never settles'. It is an accurate, fair and visible statement of the single-layer limit.

45.9-47.3 s: try 4 is RIGHT and the lantern flares, then try 5 ('a new horizontal bar · said horizontal · RIGHT') shows generalisation, an honest trace of the perceptron rule rather than a staged success.
37.6 s: on 'nudge', only the dials fed by the lit cells turn, with arrows, under 'correct answer: horizontal'. That is the error-correction rule and its supervision shown truthfully at once.
61.0-63.5 s bookend: Rosenblatt, clear of the machine now, studies the lit retina in the green lab under the returning title, a respectful last image of a real person.
